title: Electrophysiological and anatomical characterization of synaptic remodeling in the mouse whisker thalamus
protocol: Anesthetize a mouse older than 3 weeks with 2-3% isoflurane for 5 minutes.
Maintain anesthesia by intraperitoneal injection of medetomidine, midazolam, and butorphanol in saline.
Place a mouse on a heating pad set to 40°C.
Make a vertical incision between the whisker pad and the eye.
Expose the infraorbital nerve using two forceps under a microscope.
Free the infraorbital nerve from connective tissue without causing bleeding.
Locally anesthetize the nerve by applying 2% xylocaine with 1:80,000 adrenaline.
Lift the nerve up and cut it at a central site first.
Cut the nerve again at a peripheral site 1–2 mm away from the central site to prevent axonal regeneration.
Suture the skin after cutting the nerve.
Inject atipamezole (0.1 mg/kg) intraperitoneally to reverse the sedative effect of medetomidine.
Anesthetize a mouse by exposing it to 2–3% isoflurane in an anesthesia induction chamber for 5–10 minutes.
Maintain anesthesia through intraperitoneal injection of medetomidine (0.3 mg/kg), midazolam (4 mg/kg), and butorphanol (5 mg/kg) in saline.
Monitor body temperature during the operation.
Apply continuous isoflurane at 0.5–1% if the operation is expected to last longer than 25 minutes.
Return the mouse to its home cage after the procedure until the electrophysiological or histological experiment can be performed.
Place the anesthetized mouse in a stereotaxic apparatus using an auxiliary ear bar.
Apply 2% xylocaine jelly to the outer ear for local anesthesia before attaching the auxiliary ear bar.
Apply 0.3% ofloxacin gel to both eyes to protect them during the operation.
Make a skin incision to expose the skull after applying local anesthesia with 2% xylocaine jelly.
Adjust the nose position using an incisor bar until z coordinates of bregma and lambda are the same.
Drill the skull above the marked site using a micromotor system with a steel bur.
Pause drilling by cooling with saline at 20°C–25°C to reduce heat damage to the brain.
Attach a 10 μL Hamilton syringe with a stainless-steel needle to a syringe holder connected to a microprocessor-controlled injector.
Fill the injection solution into the needle from the tip.
Move the syringe to the surface of the drilled site.
Insert the needle into the target depth of the brain and inject the solution continuously.
Remove the needle.
Maintain the needle in place for at least 5 minutes after injection.
Inject using air pressure or iontophoretic delivery as needed.
Reverse sedative effect of medetomidine with intraperitoneal injection of atipamezole (0.1 mg/kg).
Return the mouse to its home cage until electrophysiological or histological experiment is performed.
Pull borosilicate glass capillaries using a single pull with a micropipette puller for iontophoretic delivery.
Adjust injection speed between 40–100 nL/min.
Cut off the tip of a pulled-pipette using scissors.
Draw the injection solution into the pipette tip by capillary action.
Backfill saline slowly using a 1-mL syringe with a flexible needle.
Insert an Ag/AgCl wire into the pipette and attach it to the pipette holder.
Move the pipette to the surface of the drilled site.
Insert the pipette into the target depth of the brain.
Apply current with 7-s on/off cycles for 20–30 min using an iontophoresis pump.
Remove the pipette.
Irontophorese a retrograde tracer, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated cholera toxin subunit B (CTB647) at 0.2% in ddH2O to the dorsal part of the thalamic ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM).
Identify VPM using VGLUT2 immunohistochemistry with a guinea pig anti-VGluT2 antibody and an Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody.
Acquire gray-scale images using an epifluorescence microscope equipped with a cooled CCD camera.
Pseudocolour images using Adobe Photoshop software.
Mix clodronate liposomes with Hamilton syringe for local injection into the brainstem.
Perform immunohistochemistry using rabbit anti-Iba1 antibody and an Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody.
Acquire gray-scale images using an epifluorescence microscope.
Invert images using Adobe Photoshop software.
Administer PLX3397 systemically to inhibit microglial proliferation across the brain.
Dilute the 10× aCSF stock solution to 1 L with ddH2O.
Add 3.6 g glucose (20 mM) to the diluted aCSF solution.
Bubble the aCSF solution with a mixture of 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Add 2 mL of 1M CaCl2 solution (2 mM) to the aCSF solution.
Add 1 mL of 1M MgCl2 solution (1 mM) to the aCSF solution.
Transfer 100–150 mL of prepared aCSF to a glass beaker and place it in the water bath set at 32°C.
Bubble this aCSF solution continuously.
Add Na-ascorbate (5 mM), Na-pyruvate (3 mM), and thiourea (2 mM) to both aCSF and cutting solution for improved neuronal recovery.
Alternatively, add lactic acid (4 mM) instead of Na-ascorbate, Na-pyruvate, and thiourea for improved neuronal recovery.
Remove Na-ascorbate, Na-pyruveate, thiourea, or lactic acid from aCSF during recording.
Perfuse 5 mL of cooled cutting solution transcardially using a 10 mL syringe with a 21-gauge needle within 1 min after deep anesthesia with isoflurane.
Decapitate the mouse quickly and remove the brain for soaking in cutting solution on ice for 1–3 min to avoid neuronal damage or death.
Trim the brain on a filter paper using a razor blade or surgical blade.
Glue the brain block onto the electrical-taped specimen disk using cyanoacrylate (Aron alpha).
Glue a block of gelatin (2-3%) behind the brain block.
Place the disk onto the buffer tray with cutting solution continuously bubbled with 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Cut sagittal slices of 250- or 300-μm thickness including the whisker thalamus (VPM) using a vibratome with a razor blade.
Collect the slices on the holding chamber in the water bath.
Incubate brain slices in the aCSF solution for 30 min at 32°C using a water bath.
Incubate brain slices for an additional 30 min at 20°C–25°C until use.
Establish a whole-cell patch on a thalamic neuron which is identified using a near-infrared camera-equipped microscope.
Maintain the temperature of aCSF at 31°C–32°C during recording.
Add GABAA receptor antagonist bicuculline methochloride (10 μM) and GABAB receptor antagonist CGP55845 hydrochloride (1 μM) to block inhibitory postsynaptic currents.
Use 5 or 6 cycles for pulling a whole-cell patch pipette using the micropipette puller.
Increase or decrease velocity in the last step to correct tip diameter.
Keep internal solution on ice during recording.
Collect slices of 250- or 300-μm thickness in a glass vial or 24-well plate after recording.
Soak collected slices into fixative solution.
Store soaked slices for 12–16 h at 4°C.
Store the slices in fixative solution at 4°C for a few weeks.
Wash the slices three times with 0.1 M PBS for 10–20 min on a shaker.
Incubate the slices with fluorescent streptavidin (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated streptavidin, 1:500) in 0.1 M PBS with 0.05% Triton X-100 for 2–3 h at 20°C–25°C or 12–16 h at 4°C.
Wash the slices two times with 0.1 M PBS for 5–10 min and then with 0.1 M PB for 5–10 min to remove NaCl.
Mount the slices on a gelatin-coated glass slide.
Seal the sections with antifade mountant and apply a coverslip.
Deeply anesthetize the Krox20-Cre : Ai34D mouse with isoflurane and place it on the shallow tray.
Make an abdominal incision on the liver and find the xiphoid process.
Lift the xiphoid process.
Expose the pleural cavity by making a lateral incision in the diaphragm.
Cut along the lateral wall of the rib cage on both sides until the heart and thymus are exposed.
Displace the lung carefully during cutting the rib cage to avoid injury.
Make a small incision in the right atrial ear.
Insert a 21-gauge needle quickly into the left ventricle connected to a peristaltic pump system.
Perfuse the fixative solution followed by 5 ml of prefixative solution at 20°C–25°C for 10–15 minutes using a peristaltic pump.
Trim the fixed brain on the brain slicer matrix using a microtome blade.
Glue the brain block onto the specimen disk using Aron Alpha.
Mount the block with agarose gel solution using a mold (20 mL cut syringe).
Allow the disk to cool to set the gel in the refrigerator.
Trim the gels and glue the mounted brain block back onto the disk.
Set the disk onto the buffer tray containing cooled 0.1 M PB.
Cool the buffer tray with ice or ice packs during cutting using a vibratome with an injector blade.
Cut sections at a speed ranging between 0.05–0.2 mm/s (scale 1–4.5 for Leica VT1000S).
Set the frequency normally at 40–50 Hz (scale 4–5).
Collect sections and submerge them into a 24-well plate with 0.1 M PB.
Use coronal sections for histological experiments to observe both brainstem and thalamus.
Set section thickness to 40 or 50 μm for handling and antibody penetration.
Use sections of 8–20 μm thickness for analyzing colocalization of different markers or labeling in individual cell somata under epifluorescence microscopy.
Wash the sections three times with 0.1 M PBS for 5–10 min in a 12-well plate on a shaker.

Incubate the sections with primary antibody (guinea pig polyclonal antibody against vesicular glutamate transporter type2 (VGluT2), 1:500 or 1,000) in 10% normal donkey serum solution with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 12–16 h at 4°C or 2–3 h at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker.
Wash the sections three times with 0.1 M PBS for 5–10 min.
Incubate the sections with secondary antibody and Fluorescent Nissl in 10% normal donkey serum solution with 0.3% Triton X-100 for 12–16 hours at 4°C or 2–3 hours at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker.
Wash the sections two times with 0.1 M PBS for 5–10 minutes and then with 0.1 M PB for 5–10 minutes.
Mount the sections on a gelatin-coated glass slide.
Seal the sections with antifade mountant and apply a coverslip.
Use spacers when sections are coverslipped for confocal microscopic observation.
Acquire images using an epifluorescent microscope or by confocal microscopy.
Use anti-Iba1 antibody for immunohistochemistry to visualize myeloid cells including microglia.
Use anti-TMEM119 antibody specifically for detecting microglia.
For lower magnification images (2×, 4×, or 5×), use an aqueous mountant without antifade reagents such as Fluoromount-G.
